speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start with your double vision: do the eyes move together normally, or does one drift when you try to focus? Also, have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or speaking along with your climbing stairs weakness?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Blood_chemistry (specifically CK, Aldolase, and Glucose). Also, please tell me if you have noticed any muscle twitching or fatigue in your eyelids specifically?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of diplopia worsening with gaze direction, pt eyelid fatigue, and proximal muscle weakness that fluctuates with activity is classic for this condition; the previous suggestion of tuberculosis does not fit the symptom profile. Please proceed with acetylcholine receptor antibody testing and a Chest_XRay to rule out thymoma.
